newsitem.title: BELGIUM: ECU BASKET RECOVERS POST AMSTERDAM SUMMIT EMU DEAL.
newsitem.headline: ECU BASKET RECOVERS POST AMSTERDAM SUMMIT EMU DEAL.

text.p: The European Currency Unit (Ecu) basket narrowed sharply its discount to its theoretical value on Tuesday morning in the wake of the Amsterdam summit deal on a single currency stability pact.
By 0800 GMT, the Ecu basket was quoted at 100.35/40, or 0.35/40 percent below its theoretical par value, compared with 100.55/60 a day earlier.
One Brussels-based market participant said the move had caught players by surprise, but appeared to be due to one large buyer of Ecu/mark rather than a general market trend.
Ecu/mark was at 1.9570/75, up from overnight levels around 1.9540.

"What we have seen this morning is one particular large buyer of Ecu. I would not say the rise is because the whole market now believes the problems (with EMU) are over -- although someone seems to think so," the trader said.
The basket Ecu has been stuck in a 100.30/60 range in the past few months. "This morning we have gone from the top to the bottom of the range. It's a big move," the trader said.

At EMU's low point during the 1992 European currency crisis the Ecu basket traded around 103.75, or 3.75 percent below its theoretical value. At the end of 1995, during a wave of strikes in France, it was around 102.75. Against the mark, the Ecu's low point was 1.807, set in March 1995 against the background of a sharp drop in the dollar.
The Ecu basket market's main players are Belgian banks Banque Paribas Belgium and Kredietbank .
